messages.content:
<question>
After the 4.2 switch to AV1, can the atlas-a1 play av1_2160p60.mkv at 60 fps?
</question>
<tool_calls>
- codec_caps {"device": "atlas-a1", "mime": "video/av01"}
  result: {"android_api_level": 36, "decoders": [{"hardware": true, "max_fps_at_max_size": 60, "max_height": 2160, "max_width": 3840, "mime": "video/av01", "name": "c2.atlas.av1.decoder", "profiles": ["Main", "Main10"]}, {"hardware": false, "max_fps_at_max_size": 20, "max_height": 2160, "max_width": 3840, "mime": "video/av01", "name": "c2.android.av1.decoder", "profiles": ["Main"]}], "device": "atlas-a1", "display_hdr_types": ["HDR10", "HLG", "HDR10+"], "max_concurrent_hw_video_decoders": 16, "mime": "video/av01", "widevine_security_level": "L1"}
- ffprobe {"file": "av1_2160p60.mkv"}
  result: {"bit_rate": 531792, "duration_s": 0.5, "file": "av1_2160p60.mkv", "format": "matroska,webm", "streams": [{"avg_frame_rate": "60/1", "codec_name": "av1", "codec_type": "video", "height": 2160, "index": 0, "pix_fmt": "yuv420p", "profile": "Main", "start_time": "0.000000", "width": 3840}]}
- search_kb {"k": 3, "query": "AV1 4K60 max frame rate decoder"}
  result: {"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "av-sync", "title": "Audio and video drift out of sync", "text": "# Audio and video drift out of sync

Players normally treat the audio clock as the master and schedule video frames against it.
Drift usually comes from wrong timestamps rather than from rendering speed.

Checks:
- Inspect stream start times and timestamps with `ffprobe -show_streams -show_frames`; a large
  `start_time` difference between audio and video streams shows up as constant offset.
- Variable-frame-rate recordings (common from phone cameras) can drift when a pipeline assumes
  a constant frame rate. Remux or transcode with correct timestamps.
- When writing a custom renderer, use `AudioTrack.getTimestamp()` to map audio frames to
  real time instead of counting written bytes."}, {"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark

HDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer
function (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and
nothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far…
</tool_calls>
<answer>
Likely cause: Yes on capability data: atlas-a1's hardware decoder c2.atlas.av1.decoder supports AV1 Main/Main10 up to 3840x2160 at 60 fps, and ffprobe shows av1_2160p60.mkv is AV1 Main, 3840x2160, 60 fps, 8-bit. The caveat is the software decoder (c2.android.av1.decoder), which tops out at 20 fps at 2160p, so 60 fps depends on the hardware decoder actually being used; I haven't seen a real playback run.
Next step: Confirm on an atlas-a1 that the player picks c2.atlas.av1.decoder (log the codec name, or `isHardwareAccelerated()` on API 29+) while playing the clip, and watch for dropped frames.
Sources: [tool:codec_caps] [tool:ffprobe] [kb:av1-decoding]
</answer>

</tool_calls>
<answer>
Likely cause: lumen-l3 reports `max_concurrent_hw_video_decoders: 4` for its only AVC hardware decoder, and the log shows ThumbGrid binding positions 0 to 3 fine, then failing at position 4 with `NO_MEMORY: max instances reached`. The log also shows `recycled position=0 but decoder not released`, so recycled thumbnails keep holding their decoder instances.
Next step: Cap the thumbnail decoder pool at no more than 4 on this device, and in practice at 3 or fewer if anything else in the app (such as a player) also needs a hardware AVC decoder. Read the limit per device from `MediaCodecInfo` capabilities rather than hard-coding it, and release or reuse a decoder when its item is recycled, so the pool size, not the scroll position, decides how many instances are alive.
Sources: [tool:logcat_grep] [tool:codec_caps]
</answer>

Example 2:
<question>
can the lumen-l3 play the 4k hdr stuff or nah. we want to know before we push it to the phone
</question>
<tool_calls>
- codec_caps {"device": "lumen-l3", "mime": "video/hevc"}
  result: {"android_api_level": 33, "decoders": [{"hardware": true, "max_fps_at_max_size": 60, "max_height": 1080, "max_width": 1920, "mime": "video/hevc", "name": "c2.lumen.hevc.decoder", "profiles": ["Main"]}], "device": "lumen-l3", "display_hdr_types": [], "max_concurrent_hw_video_decoders": 4, "mime": "video/hevc", "widevine_security_level": "L3"}
</tool_calls>
<answer>
Likely cause: Not for 4K HDR HEVC, going by the lookup. lumen-l3's only HEVC decoder (c2.lumen.hevc.decoder, hardware) tops out at 1920x1080 at 60 fps and lists only the "Main" profile (no Main10, which HDR10 needs), and the device reports no supported display HDR types. So it can't decode 2160p HEVC, and it has no HDR display path either. I only looked up HEVC; other codecs (such as AV1 or VP9) were not checked.
Next step: Before pushing to the phone, serve it an SDR rendition at 1080p or below (8-bit Main HEVC or H.264) rather than the 4K HDR one; if you need to know about another codec, run the capability lookup for that MIME type too.
Sources: [tool:codec_caps]
</answer>
Output: {"critique": "The answer says the fifth decoder allocation fails with NO_MEMORY and that the lumen-l3 allows 4 concurrent hardware decoders; the log and codec_caps show exactly that. No claim contradicts the tools.", "verdict": "PASS"}

Example 3:
<question>
one of our HDR10 test files comes out with flat colours on one of the test phones but not the others. The HDR path looks like it's engaging. What's the minimal repro we should use to tell whether the decode, the surface color space, or the display HDR capability is the culprit?
</question>
<tool_calls>
- search_kb {"k": 2, "query": "HDR10 flat colours decode vs surface colour space vs display HDR capability"}
  result: {"results": [{"id": "hdr-tone-mapping", "title": "HDR video looks washed out or too dark", "text": "# HDR video looks washed out or too dark\n\nHDR10 and HLG streams carry a wide colour gamut (BT.2020) and a high-dynamic-range transfer\nfunction (PQ or HLG). When such a stream reaches a display path that is not HDR-capable and\nnothing tone-maps it, colours look flat and grey or the picture looks far too dark.\n\nChecks:\n- Ask the display what it supports: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` (or `Display.isHdr()` on API 26+).\n- Render to a `SurfaceView`. `TextureView` composites through the GPU and is a common reason\n  HDR output gets flattened.\n- Confirm the decoder output format reports the expected colour transfer\n  (`MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER`) and colour standard.\n- If the display is SDR, tone-map explicitly (for example with a Media3 Transformer or\n  effect pipeline) or serve an SDR rendition."}, {"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android\n\nAndroid ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10\n(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many\ndevices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow\nfor high resolutions or frame rates.\n\nChecks:\n- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.\n- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is\n  hardware backed.\n- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates\n  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}]}
</tool_calls>
<answer>
Likely cause: One phone flattening an HDR10 (BT.2020/PQ) clip while others don't points to something device-specific in the path from decoder to panel: that phone's display may not report HDR, its decoder output may have lost the colour transfer, or the render path (a TextureView instead of a SurfaceView) may be flattening it. The knowledge base lists exactly these three suspects, but I haven't run anything against your file or devices, so none is confirmed.
Next step: Use one minimal repro: play the same HDR10 file on a bare SurfaceView-only activity (no TextureView, no effects) on the bad phone and a good phone, and log three things on each: `Display.getHdrCapabilities()` / `Display.isHdr()`, the decoder output `MediaFormat.KEY_COLOR_TRANSFER` and colour standard, and the surface type. A different display HDR result on the bad phone means the panel; a different or missing transfer means the decoder; if both match the good phone and a SurfaceView fixes it, the render path is at fault.
Sources: [kb:hdr-tone-mapping]
</answer>

After switching our player to AV1 in 4.2, the vela-v2 shows a black frame before AV1 playback starts. Is AV1 supported there?
</question>

  result: {"results": [{"id": "av1-decoding", "title": "AV1 decoding support on Android", "text": "# AV1 decoding support on Android

Android ships a software AV1 decoder (`c2.android.av1.decoder`) starting with Android 10
(API 29). Hardware AV1 decoding depends on the device's SoC, not on the Android version: many
devices on recent Android releases still decode AV1 in software only, which can be too slow
for high resolutions or frame rates.

Checks:
- Enumerate `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` for the MIME type `video/av01`.
- On API 29+, `MediaCodecInfo.isHardwareAccelerated()` tells you whether a decoder is
  hardware backed.
- Use `CodecCapabilities.getVideoCapabilities()` to check supported sizes and frame rates
  before choosing an AV1 rendition; fall back to VP9 or H.264/HEVC when needed."}, {"id": "mp4-faststart", "title": "Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)", "text": "# Progressive MP4 takes long to start (moov atom at the end)

An MP4 file's index (the `moov` atom) is often written at the end of the file by recorders and
encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

Checks and fix:
- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.
- Remux with the index at the front: `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4`.
- For adaptive streaming, prefer fragmented MP4 (DASH or HLS) instead."}, {"id": "widevine-levels", "title": "Widevine security levels and HD playback", "text": "# Widevine security levels and HD playback

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel"…
</tool_calls>
<answer>
Likely cause: I can't confirm AV1 support on vela-v2: codec_caps returned an error because the device profile doesn't exist (only atlas-a1 and lumen-l3 are available), and the knowledge base has no entry that explains a black frame before playback. All it offers is that a software AV1 decoder ships from API 29 and that hardware AV1 depends on the SoC.
Next step: On a vela-v2, check which video/av01 decoders `MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.REGULAR_CODECS)` returns and whether they are hardware (`isHardwareAccelerated()`, API 29+), and log the decoder name and time to first frame before and after 4.2 to see whether the decoder choice changed.
Sources: [kb:av1-decoding]
</answer>

encoders. A progressive-download player must then fetch the end of the file before playback can
begin, which shows up as a long start delay or extra range requests.

- `ffprobe -v trace file.mp4 2>&1 | grep -m2 -E "type:'(moov|mdat)'"` shows which atom comes first.

Widevine has security levels: L1 (decryption and decoding inside a hardware trusted
environment) and L3 (software only). Content owners commonly restrict HD and higher
renditions to L1, so the same app may get only SD on an L3 device.

Checks:
- Read `MediaDrm(WIDEVINE_UUID).getPropertyString("securityLevel"…
</tool_calls>
